# dggevx

> Computes for a pair of N-by-N real nonsymmetric matrices (A,B) the generalized eigenvalues, and, optionally, the left and/or right generalized eigenvectors, along with optional balancing (ILO/IHI/LSCALE/RSCALE/ABNRM/BBNRM) and reciprocal condition numbers (RCONDE/RCONDV).

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import dggevx from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/dggevx';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
dggevx(
    order,
    balanc, jobvl, jobvr, sense,
    N,
    A, LDA,
    B, LDB,
    ALPHAR, strideALPHAR,
    ALPHAI, strideALPHAI,
    BETA, strideBETA,
    VL, LDVL,
    VR, LDVR,
    ilo,
    ihi,
    LSCALE, strideLSCALE,
    RSCALE, strideRSCALE,
    abnrm,
    bbnrm,
    RCONDE, strideRCONDE,
    RCONDV, strideRCONDV,
    work,
    iwork,
    bwork
) → integer
```

Computes for a pair of N-by-N real nonsymmetric matrices (A,B) the generalized eigenvalues, and optionally, the left and/or right generalized eigenvectors.

When `work`, `iwork`, or `bwork` are `null`, this LAPACKE-style wrapper
allocates workspace arrays as a convenience (`work` of the optimal size).
Prefer passing caller-owned buffers for batched use.

| param | type | intent | shape | constraints | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `order` | `Layout` | in |  | one of `'row-major'`, `'column-major'` | storage layout (`'row-major'` or `'column-major'`) |
| `balanc` | `("none"\|"permute"\|"scale"\|"both")` | in |  | one of `'both'`, `'none'`, `'permute'`, `'scale'` | balancing option (`'none'`, `'permute'`, `'scale'`, or `'both'`) |
| `jobvl` | `("no-vectors"\|"compute-vectors")` | in |  | one of `'no-vectors'`, `'compute-vectors'` | `'compute-vectors'` or `'no-vectors'` |
| `jobvr` | `("no-vectors"\|"compute-vectors")` | in |  | one of `'no-vectors'`, `'compute-vectors'` | `'compute-vectors'` or `'no-vectors'` |
| `sense` | `("none"\|"eigenvalues"\|"right-vectors"\|"both")` | in |  | one of `'both'`, `'eigenvalues'`, `'none'`, `'right-vectors'` | reciprocal condition numbers to compute (`'none'`, `'eigenvalues'`, `'right-vectors'`, or `'both'`) |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  | requires `N ≥ 0` | order of matrices A and B |
| `A` | `Float64Array` | in/out | `N × N` |  | input matrix A (N x N), overwritten on exit |
| ↳ `LDA` | `PositiveInteger` | in |  | requires `LDA ≥ max( 1, N )` | leading dimension of A |
| `B` | `Float64Array` | in/out | `N × N` |  | input matrix B (N x N), overwritten on exit |
| ↳ `LDB` | `PositiveInteger` | in |  | requires `LDB ≥ max( 1, N )` | leading dimension of B |
| `ALPHAR` | `Float64Array` | out | `N` |  | output: real parts of alpha (length N) |
| ↳ `strideALPHAR` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for ALPHAR |
| `ALPHAI` | `Float64Array` | out | `N` |  | output: imaginary parts of alpha (length N) |
| ↳ `strideALPHAI` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for ALPHAI |
| `BETA` | `Float64Array` | out | `N` |  | output: beta values (length N) |
| ↳ `strideBETA` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for BETA |
| `VL` | `Float64Array` | out | `N × N` |  | output: left eigenvectors (N x N) |
| ↳ `LDVL` | `PositiveInteger` | in |  | rejects `ldvl < 1 \|\| ((jobvl === 'compute-vectors') && ldvl < N)` | leading dimension of VL |
| `VR` | `Float64Array` | out | `N × N` |  | output: right eigenvectors (N x N) |
| ↳ `LDVR` | `PositiveInteger` | in |  | rejects `ldvr < 1 \|\| ((jobvr === 'compute-vectors') && ldvr < N)` | leading dimension of VR |
| `ilo` | `Int32Array` | out |  |  | output (length-1 array): `ilo` |
| `ihi` | `Int32Array` | out |  |  | output (length-1 array): iLO and IHI are integer values such that on exit A(i,j) = 0 and B(i,j) = 0 if i > j and j = 1,...,ILO-1 or i = IHI+1,...,N |
| `LSCALE` | `Float64Array` | out | `N` |  | output: permutation/scaling factors (length N) |
| ↳ `strideLSCALE` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for LSCALE |
| `RSCALE` | `Float64Array` | out | `N` |  | output: permutation/scaling factors (length N) |
| ↳ `strideRSCALE` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for RSCALE |
| `abnrm` | `Float64Array` | out |  |  | output (length-1 array): the one-norm of the balanced matrix A |
| `bbnrm` | `Float64Array` | out |  |  | output (length-1 array): the one-norm of the balanced matrix B |
| `RCONDE` | `Float64Array` | out | `N` |  | output: reciprocal condition numbers of eigenvalues (length N) |
| ↳ `strideRCONDE` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for RCONDE |
| `RCONDV` | `Float64Array` | out | `N` |  | output: reciprocal condition numbers of right eigenvectors (length N) |
| ↳ `strideRCONDV` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for RCONDV |
| `work` | `(Float64Array\|null)` | out | `≥ MINWRK` |  | real workspace of length at least `2*N` if `balanc` is 'none' or 'permute' and no eigenvectors are computed, else `6*N`; at least `10*N` if `sense` is 'eigenvalues' or 'both'; at least `2*N*(N+4)+16` if `sense` is 'right-vectors' or 'both' (all at least 1). For optimal performance at least `max( minimum, N + N*NB + TSIZE )` (`NB` from `ilaenv`, `TSIZE = 4160`), the reference's `N + N*NB` with the dormqr optimum's T part, which enables the blocked QR steps; or `null` to allocate the optimal size |
| `iwork` | `(Int32Array\|null)` | out | `≥ N + 6` |  | caller-provided integer workspace of length max(1,N+6), or `null` to auto-allocate; not referenced when sense='none' or 'eigenvalues' |
| `bwork` | `(Uint8Array\|null)` | out | `≥ N` |  | caller-provided logical workspace of length max(1,N), or `null` to auto-allocate; not referenced when sense='none' |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `balanc`: Specifies the balance option to be performed.

  -   `= 'N'`: do not diagonally scale or permute;
  -   `= 'P'`: permute only;
  -   `= 'S'`: scale only;
  -   `= 'B'`: both permute and scale. Computed reciprocal condition numbers will be for the matrices after permuting and/or balancing. Permuting does not change condition numbers (in exact arithmetic), but balancing does.
- `jobvl`:

  -   `= 'N'`: do not compute the left generalized eigenvectors;
  -   `= 'V'`: compute the left generalized eigenvectors.
- `jobvr`:

  -   `= 'N'`: do not compute the right generalized eigenvectors;
  -   `= 'V'`: compute the right generalized eigenvectors.
- `sense`: Determines which reciprocal condition numbers are computed.

  -   `= 'N'`: none are computed;
  -   `= 'E'`: computed for eigenvalues only;
  -   `= 'V'`: computed for eigenvectors only;
  -   `= 'B'`: computed for eigenvalues and eigenvectors.
- `N`: The order of the matrices A, B, `VL`, and `VR`. $N \ge 0$.
- `A`: On entry, the matrix A in the pair (A,B). On exit, A has been overwritten. If `JOBVL='V'` or `JOBVR='V'` or both, then A contains the first part of the real Schur form of the "balanced" versions of the input A and B.
- `B`: On entry, the matrix B in the pair (A,B). On exit, B has been overwritten. If `JOBVL='V'` or `JOBVR='V'` or both, then B contains the second part of the real Schur form of the "balanced" versions of the input A and B.
- `BETA`: On exit, (`ALPHAR(j)` + `ALPHAI(j)`\*i)/`BETA(j)`, $j=1$,...,N, will be the generalized eigenvalues. If `ALPHAI(j)` is zero, then the j-th eigenvalue is real; if positive, then the j-th and (j+1)-st eigenvalues are a complex conjugate pair, with `ALPHAI(j+1)` negative.

  Note: the quotients `ALPHAR(j)`/`BETA(j)` and `ALPHAI(j)`/`BETA(j)` may easily over- or underflow, and `BETA(j)` may even be zero. Thus, the user should avoid naively computing the ratio ALPHA/`BETA`. However, `ALPHAR` and `ALPHAI` will be always less than and usually comparable with norm(A) in magnitude, and `BETA` always less than and usually comparable with norm(B).
- `VL`: If `JOBVL = 'V'`, the left eigenvectors u(j) are stored one after another in the columns of `VL`, in the same order as their eigenvalues. If the j-th eigenvalue is real, then $u(j) = \mathrm{VL}(:,j)$, the j-th column of `VL`. If the j-th and (j+1)-th eigenvalues form a complex conjugate pair, then $u(j) = \mathrm{VL}(:,j)+i \, \mathrm{VL}(:,j+1)$ and $u(j+1) = \mathrm{VL}(:,j)-i \, \mathrm{VL}(:,j+1)$. Each eigenvector will be scaled so the largest component have abs(real part) + abs(imag. part) = 1. Not referenced if `JOBVL = 'N'`.
- `VR`: If `JOBVR = 'V'`, the right eigenvectors v(j) are stored one after another in the columns of `VR`, in the same order as their eigenvalues. If the j-th eigenvalue is real, then $v(j) = \mathrm{VR}(:,j)$, the j-th column of `VR`. If the j-th and (j+1)-th eigenvalues form a complex conjugate pair, then $v(j) = \mathrm{VR}(:,j)+i \, \mathrm{VR}(:,j+1)$ and $v(j+1) = \mathrm{VR}(:,j)-i \, \mathrm{VR}(:,j+1)$. Each eigenvector will be scaled so the largest component have abs(real part) + abs(imag. part) = 1. Not referenced if `JOBVR = 'N'`.
- `ihi`: `ILO` and `IHI` are integer values such that on exit $A(i,j) = 0$ and $B(i,j) = 0$ if $i > j$ and $j = 1$,...,`ILO`-1 or $i = \mathrm{IHI}+1$,...,N. If `BALANC = 'N'` or 'S', `ILO = 1` and `IHI = N`.
- `LSCALE`: Details of the permutations and scaling factors applied to the left side of A and B. If PL(j) is the index of the row interchanged with row j, and DL(j) is the scaling factor applied to row j, then

  $$
  \mathrm{LSCALE}(j) = \mathrm{PL}(j) \quad\text{for}\quad j = 1, \cdots ,\mathrm{ILO}-1
  $$

  $$
  = \mathrm{DL}(j) \quad\text{for}\quad j = \mathrm{ILO}, \cdots ,\mathrm{IHI}
  $$

  $$
  = \mathrm{PL}(j) \quad\text{for}\quad j = \mathrm{IHI}+1, \cdots ,N
  $$

  The order in which the interchanges are made is N to `IHI`+1, then 1 to `ILO`-1.
- `RSCALE`: Details of the permutations and scaling factors applied to the right side of A and B. If PR(j) is the index of the column interchanged with column j, and DR(j) is the scaling factor applied to column j, then

  $$
  \mathrm{RSCALE}(j) = \mathrm{PR}(j) \quad\text{for}\quad j = 1, \cdots ,\mathrm{ILO}-1
  $$

  $$
  = \mathrm{DR}(j) \quad\text{for}\quad j = \mathrm{ILO}, \cdots ,\mathrm{IHI}
  $$

  $$
  = \mathrm{PR}(j) \quad\text{for}\quad j = \mathrm{IHI}+1, \cdots ,N
  $$

  The order in which the interchanges are made is N to `IHI`+1, then 1 to `ILO`-1.
- `abnrm`: The one-norm of the balanced matrix A.
- `bbnrm`: The one-norm of the balanced matrix B.
- `RCONDE`: If `SENSE = 'E'` or 'B', the reciprocal condition numbers of the eigenvalues, stored in consecutive elements of the array. For a complex conjugate pair of eigenvalues two consecutive elements of `RCONDE` are set to the same value. Thus `RCONDE(j)`, `RCONDV(j)`, and the j-th columns of `VL` and `VR` all correspond to the j-th eigenpair. If `SENSE` = 'N or 'V', `RCONDE` is not referenced.
- `RCONDV`: If `SENSE = 'V'` or 'B', the estimated reciprocal condition numbers of the eigenvectors, stored in consecutive elements of the array. For a complex eigenvector two consecutive elements of `RCONDV` are set to the same value. If the eigenvalues cannot be reordered to compute `RCONDV(j)`, `RCONDV(j)` is set to 0; this can only occur when the true value would be very small anyway. If `SENSE = 'N'` or 'E', `RCONDV` is not referenced.
- `work`: On exit, if `INFO = 0`, `WORK(1)` returns the optimal `LWORK`.
- `iwork`: If `SENSE = 'E'`, `IWORK` is not referenced.
- `bwork`: If `SENSE = 'N'`, `BWORK` is not referenced.

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: status code (0 = success)

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be a valid order
- `TypeError` second argument must be one of the following: "both", "none", "permute", "scale"
- `TypeError` third argument must be one of the following: "no-vectors", "compute-vectors"
- `TypeError` fourth argument must be one of the following: "no-vectors", "compute-vectors"
- `TypeError` fifth argument must be one of the following: "both", "eigenvalues", "none", "right-vectors"
- `RangeError` sixth argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` eighth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, N )`
- `RangeError` tenth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, N )`
- `RangeError` eighteenth argument is invalid (rejected when `LDVL < 1 \|\| ( ( jobvl === "compute-vectors" ) && LDVL < N )`)
- `RangeError` twentieth argument is invalid (rejected when `LDVR < 1 \|\| ( ( jobvr === "compute-vectors" ) && LDVR < N )`)

### Strided (ndarray) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
dggevx.ndarray(
    balanc, jobvl, jobvr, sense,
    N,
    A, strideA1, strideA2, offsetA,
    B, strideB1, strideB2, offsetB,
    ALPHAR, strideALPHAR, offsetALPHAR,
    ALPHAI, strideALPHAI, offsetALPHAI,
    BETA, strideBETA, offsetBETA,
    VL, strideVL1, strideVL2, offsetVL,
    VR, strideVR1, strideVR2, offsetVR,
    ilo,
    ihi,
    LSCALE, strideLSCALE, offsetLSCALE,
    RSCALE, strideRSCALE, offsetRSCALE,
    abnrm,
    bbnrm,
    RCONDE, strideRCONDE, offsetRCONDE,
    RCONDV, strideRCONDV, offsetRCONDV,
    work, strideWork, offsetWork,
    iwork, strideIwork, offsetIwork,
    bwork, strideBwork, offsetBwork
) → integer
```

Computes for a pair of N-by-N real nonsymmetric matrices (A,B) the generalized eigenvalues, and optionally, the left and/or right generalized eigenvectors.

Matrix shapes are logical (rows × columns). The reference's leading dimension (`LDA`, …) is replaced by the two strides and the offset.

| param | type | intent | shape | constraints | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `balanc` | `("none"\|"permute"\|"scale"\|"both")` | in |  | one of `'both'`, `'none'`, `'permute'`, `'scale'` | balancing option (`'none'`, `'permute'`, `'scale'`, or `'both'`) |
| `jobvl` | `("no-vectors"\|"compute-vectors")` | in |  | one of `'no-vectors'`, `'compute-vectors'` | `'compute-vectors'` or `'no-vectors'` |
| `jobvr` | `("no-vectors"\|"compute-vectors")` | in |  | one of `'no-vectors'`, `'compute-vectors'` | `'compute-vectors'` or `'no-vectors'` |
| `sense` | `("none"\|"eigenvalues"\|"right-vectors"\|"both")` | in |  | one of `'both'`, `'eigenvalues'`, `'none'`, `'right-vectors'` | reciprocal condition numbers to compute (`'none'`, `'eigenvalues'`, `'right-vectors'`, or `'both'`) |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  | requires `N ≥ 0` | order of matrices A and B |
| `A` | `Float64Array` | in/out | `N × N` |  | input matrix A (N x N), overwritten on exit |
| ↳ `strideA1` | `integer` | in |  |  | first dimension stride of A |

If the j-th and (j+1)-th eigenvalues form a complex conjugate pair, then $v(j) = \mathrm{VR}(:,j)+i \, \mathrm{VR}(:,j+1)$ and $v(j+1) = \mathrm{VR}(:,j)-i \, \mathrm{VR}(:,j+1)$. Each eigenvector will be scaled so the largest component have abs(real part) + abs(imag. part) = 1. Not referenced if `JOBVR = 'N'`.
- `ihi`: `ILO` and `IHI` are integer values such that on exit $A(i,j) = 0$ and $B(i,j) = 0$ if $i > j$ and $j = 1$,...,`ILO`-1 or $i = \mathrm{IHI}+1$,...,N. If `BALANC = 'N'` or 'S', `ILO = 1` and `IHI = N`.
- `LSCALE`: Details of the permutations and scaling factors applied to the left side of A and B. If PL(j) is the index of the row interchanged with row j, and DL(j) is the scaling factor applied to row j, then

  $$
  \mathrm{LSCALE}(j) = \mathrm{PL}(j) \quad\text{for}\quad j = 1, \cdots ,\mathrm{ILO}-1
  $$

  $$
  = \mathrm{DL}(j) \quad\text{for}\quad j = \mathrm{ILO}, \cdots ,\mathrm{IHI}
  $$

  $$
  = \mathrm{PL}(j) \quad\text{for}\quad j = \mathrm{IHI}+1, \cdots ,N
  $$

  The order in which the interchanges are made is N to `IHI`+1, then 1 to `ILO`-1.
- `RSCALE`: Details of the permutations and scaling factors applied to the right side of A and B. If PR(j) is the index of the column interchanged with column j, and DR(j) is the scaling factor applied to column j, then

  $$
  \mathrm{RSCALE}(j) = \mathrm{PR}(j) \quad\text{for}\quad j = 1, \cdots ,\mathrm{ILO}-1
  $$

  $$
  = \mathrm{DR}(j) \quad\text{for}\quad j = \mathrm{ILO}, \cdots ,\mathrm{IHI}
  $$

  $$
  = \mathrm{PR}(j) \quad\text{for}\quad j = \mathrm{IHI}+1, \cdots ,N
  $$

  The order in which the interchanges are made is N to `IHI`+1, then 1 to `ILO`-1.
- `abnrm`: The one-norm of the balanced matrix A.
- `bbnrm`: The one-norm of the balanced matrix B.
- `RCONDE`: If `SENSE = 'E'` or 'B', the reciprocal condition numbers of the eigenvalues, stored in consecutive elements of the array. For a complex conjugate pair of eigenvalues two consecutive elements of `RCONDE` are set to the same value. Thus `RCONDE(j)`, `RCONDV(j)`, and the j-th columns of `VL` and `VR` all correspond to the j-th eigenpair. If `SENSE` = 'N or 'V', `RCONDE` is not referenced.
- `RCONDV`: If `SENSE = 'V'` or 'B', the estimated reciprocal condition numbers of the eigenvectors, stored in consecutive elements of the array. For a complex eigenvector two consecutive elements of `RCONDV` are set to the same value. If the eigenvalues cannot be reordered to compute `RCONDV(j)`, `RCONDV(j)` is set to 0; this can only occur when the true value would be very small anyway. If `SENSE = 'N'` or 'E', `RCONDV` is not referenced.
- `work`: On exit, if `INFO = 0`, `WORK(1)` returns the optimal `LWORK`.
- `iwork`: If `SENSE = 'E'`, `IWORK` is not referenced.
- `bwork`: If `SENSE = 'N'`, `BWORK` is not referenced.

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: status code (0 = success)

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be one of the following: "both", "none", "permute", "scale"
- `TypeError` second argument must be one of the following: "no-vectors", "compute-vectors"
- `TypeError` third argument must be one of the following: "no-vectors", "compute-vectors"
- `TypeError` fourth argument must be one of the following: "both", "eigenvalues", "none", "right-vectors"
- `RangeError` fifth argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `TypeError` invalid balanc value
- `TypeError` invalid jobvl value
- `TypeError` invalid jobvr value
- `TypeError` invalid sense value
- `RangeError` N must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` work array must be large enough
- `RangeError` iwork array must be large enough
- `RangeError` bwork array must be large enough

### Status codes

An `info` status code: `0` on success. A positive value reports a numerical condition such as a singular pivot or a failure to converge (see the description). Invalid arguments throw instead of returning a negative `info`. Returns immediately when `N === 0`.

The reference documents `INFO` as:

-   `= 0`: successful exit
-   `< 0`: if `INFO = -i`, the i-th argument had an illegal value.
-   `= 1,...,N`:  The QZ iteration failed.  No eigenvectors have been calculated, but `ALPHAR(j)`, `ALPHAI(j)`, and `BETA(j)` should be correct for $j=\mathrm{INFO}+1$,...,N.
-   `> N`: =N+1: other than QZ iteration failed in DHGEQZ. =N+2: error return from DTGEVC.

</section>

<!-- /.usage -->

<section class="notes">

## Notes

-   `dggevx()` corresponds to the reference LAPACK routine [`DGGEVX`](https://github.com/Reference-LAPACK/lapack/blob/v3.12.0/SRC/dggevx.f).
-   Workspace (`WORK`, `IWORK`, `BWORK`) is allocated internally; there is no `LWORK` parameter.

</section>

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import Float64Array from '@stdlib/array/float64/lib/index.js';
import Int32Array from '@stdlib/array/int32/lib/index.js';
import dggevx from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/dggevx';

const ilo = new Int32Array( 1 );
const ihi = new Int32Array( 1 );
const abnrm = new Float64Array( 1 );
const bbnrm = new Float64Array( 1 );

const N = 2;
const A = new Float64Array( [ 2.0, 0.0, 0.0, 5.0 ] );
const B = new Float64Array( [ 1.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0 ] );
const ALPHAR = new Float64Array( N );
const ALPHAI = new Float64Array( N );
const BETA = new Float64Array( N );
const VL = new Float64Array( 1 );
const VR = new Float64Array( 1 );
const LSCALE = new Float64Array( N );
const RSCALE = new Float64Array( N );
const RCONDE = new Float64Array( N );
const RCONDV = new Float64Array( N );

const out = {
	'info': dggevx( 'column-major', 'none', 'no-vectors', 'no-vectors', 'none', N, A, N, B, N, ALPHAR, 1, ALPHAI, 1, BETA, 1, VL, 1, VR, 1, ilo, ihi, LSCALE, 1, RSCALE, 1, abnrm, bbnrm, RCONDE, 1, RCONDV, 1, null, null, null ),
	'ilo': ilo[ 0 ],
	'ihi': ihi[ 0 ],
	'abnrm': abnrm[ 0 ],
	'bbnrm': bbnrm[ 0 ]
};
console.log( out ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
console.log( 'eigenvalue 0:', ALPHAR[ 0 ] / BETA[ 0 ] ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
console.log( 'eigenvalue 1:', ALPHAR[ 1 ] / BETA[ 1 ] ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `DGGEVX`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

DGGEVX computes for a pair of N-by-N real nonsymmetric matrices (A,B) the generalized eigenvalues, and optionally, the left and/or right generalized eigenvectors.

Optionally also, it computes a balancing transformation to improve the conditioning of the eigenvalues and eigenvectors (`ILO`, `IHI`, `LSCALE`, `RSCALE`, `ABNRM`, and `BBNRM`), reciprocal condition numbers for the eigenvalues (`RCONDE`), and reciprocal condition numbers for the right eigenvectors (`RCONDV`).

A generalized eigenvalue for a pair of matrices (A,B) is a scalar $\lambda$ or a ratio $\alpha /\beta = \lambda$, such that $A - \lambda \, B$ is singular. It is usually represented as the pair ($\alpha$,$\beta$), as there is a reasonable interpretation for $\beta =0$, and even for both being zero.

The right eigenvector v(j) corresponding to the eigenvalue lambda(j) of (A,B) satisfies

$$
A \, v(j) = \lambda (j) \, B \, v(j)
$$

The left eigenvector u(j) corresponding to the eigenvalue lambda(j) of (A,B) satisfies

$$
u(j)^H \, A = \lambda (j) \, u(j)^H \, B
$$

where $u(j)^H$ is the conjugate-transpose of u(j).

### Further Details

Balancing a matrix pair (A,B) includes, first, permuting rows and columns to isolate eigenvalues, second, applying diagonal similarity transformation to the rows and columns to make the rows and columns as close in norm as possible. The computed reciprocal condition numbers correspond to the balanced matrix. Permuting rows and columns will not change the condition numbers (in exact arithmetic) but diagonal scaling will. For further explanation of balancing, see section 4.11.1.2 of LAPACK Users' Guide.

An approximate error bound on the chordal distance between the i-th computed generalized eigenvalue w and the corresponding exact eigenvalue $\lambda$ is

chord(w, $\lambda$) \<= $\mathrm{EPS} \, \operatorname{norm}(\mathrm{ABNRM}, \mathrm{BBNRM}) / \mathrm{RCONDE}(I)$

An approximate error bound for the angle between the i-th computed eigenvector `VL(i)` or `VR(i)` is given by

$$
\mathrm{EPS} \, \operatorname{norm}(\mathrm{ABNRM}, \mathrm{BBNRM}) / \mathrm{DIF}(i)
$$

For further explanation of the reciprocal condition numbers `RCONDE` and `RCONDV`, see section 4.11 of LAPACK User's Guide.

</section>
